ruling.recommended_action: Refund $10.36 to the rider as a Ryde voucher for the unexempted detour distance on this RydeTAXI trip; note the driver's RD-1 shortest-route breach on file (no account flag — no prior upheld route dispute).

segment_findings.reason: Off-route segment 09:12–09:26 added 7.35 km (9.41 km vs 2.05 km optimal), max 1333 m off the optimal route. No rider consent exists: there are no in-app chat messages [F7] and the driver's post-trip claim of a flooding detour is a statement, not consent (RD-5 / G11). RD-4(a) fails because no traffic incident is recorded in the trip window [F12]; RD-4(b) is corroboration only and cannot exempt on its own — the Ayer Rajah band-2 record [F9] ends exactly when the detour began, and the other roads were band 4 [F10][F11]. Heavy rain [F13] is context only. Segment not exempted → RD-2 refund.

rejected_claims.reason: Driver's claim that the detour was forced by congestion/flooding: RD-4 requires a DataMall incident on the replaced optimal stretch and none was recorded [F12]; a single band-2 speed record [F9] is corroboration only under RD-4(b)/G3, and the alternative roads were free-flowing [F10][F11]. Also, a post-trip written statement is not before-the-fact rider consent under RD-5.

No rider consent to the routing change: there are zero in-app chat messages [F7]; the driver's assertion that 'any driver would have done the same' is not evidence of the rider agreeing to this segment (RD-5, G11).
